provenance.prompt:
Edit Image 1 only as a tightly constrained Dino Atlas local head-surface repair for Tarbosaurus bataar. Image 2 is the approved project-owned skull and skin control. Preserve Image 1's exact square frame, high front-left three-quarter composition, camera, scale, lighting, habitat, palette, head length and width, eyes, nostrils, jaws, teeth, neck, torso, exactly two separate tiny forearms, both two-fingered hands, exactly two hind legs, both three-principal-toed feet, pelvis, and complete single tail. Do not reframe, mirror, crop, recolor, change the pose or change any area except the top surface of the skull.

Repair only the skull roof from the nasal bridge to the rear cranium. Remove every large triangular spike, sawtooth, horn and raised crest. Replace them with a low continuous natural tyrannosaurid skull contour covered in small rounded pebbled scales like Image 2. Keep only subtle low rounded scale bosses that remain flush with the head silhouette; no spike row, no comb, no horn, no allosauroid lacrimal crest and no dragon ornament. Retain the long, relatively narrow but still deep Tarbosaurus skull, the existing facial proportions, eye, nostril, mouth and restrained teal/rust facial markings.

Maintain exactly two hands with exactly two functional fingers and two claw tips per hand, two legs, two feet with three forward weight-bearing principal toes each, and one pelvis-connected tail. No added animal, extra limb, hidden hand, third finger, fused foot, split tail, text, logo, watermark, fantasy anatomy, external artwork imitation or named-artist style. Natural-history museum realism for children ages 5–14.
